html:
The Kandyan Convention was the treaty signed at Kandy on 2 March 1815 by which the chiefs of the Kingdom of Kandy accepted British rule. It ended the long line of Sinhalese kings.

The chiefs had turned against their king, Sri Vikrama Rajasinha, and let British troops in. The treaty deposed him, and he died in exile in India. It promised to protect Buddhism and keep Kandyan law and the chiefs' rights. For the first time one power held the whole island, as British Ceylon.

The Uva Rebellion of 1817 and 1818 was crushed harshly. The British then built roads into the hills and cleared the forests for coffee and later tea, worked by Tamil labourers brought from India.
